claims.text: Resistance to time-dependent plastic deformation is governed by a synergy between multilayer architecture and lattice distortion from multiple principal elements.
Multilayer architecture and lattice distortion inhibit dislocation motion and delay creep under sustained load.
FeCoNiMnCu HEA coatings can be used on an SS-304 substrate.
The as-deposited coating has a multilayer structure with established layer interfaces.
The as-deposited FeCoNiMnCu-based coating exhibits intrinsic lattice distortion.
Multilayer and monolithic HEA coatings should be compared under identical elevated-temperature, constant-stress creep conditions.
Interfaces between layers impede dislocation propagation.
Local lattice distortions associated with the HEA composition disrupt dislocation motion.
The multilayer architecture creates periodic stress fields.
The HEA is a nearly equiatomic multicomponent alloy.
The multicomponent HEA exhibits sluggish diffusion.
Interfacial barriers, sluggish diffusion, and lattice distortion act synergistically to reduce dislocation mobility and slow time-dependent plastic deformation.
Under identical high-temperature stress, the multilayer coating will have a significantly lower creep strain rate than a monolithic HEA coating.
The multilayer coating will accumulate less plastic deformation than the monolithic coating.
The proposed mechanism applies only over temperature and stress ranges that avoid phase transformation and significant oxidation.
At extreme temperatures or in corrosive environments, degradation mechanisms other than interface-controlled dislocation resistance may dominate.
The relative quantitative contributions of multilayer interfaces and intrinsic lattice distortion to creep resistance are not established.
Failure to observe a statistically significant reduction in creep strain rate and accumulated plastic deformation in the multilayer coating would falsify the proposed hypothesis.
